subject: biology
title: Cell Biology Adventure 2: Membranes — Davson-Danielli to Fluid Mosaic
welcome_lead: Today you'll trace the plasma membrane from sandwich model to fluid mosaic.
meta_desc: Biology — membrane structure, phospholipid bilayer, Singer-Nicolson fluid mosaic, transport mechanisms.
final_note: You learned the fluid mosaic replaced Davson-Danielli, and that membranes transport via diffusion, osmosis, facilitated diffusion and active transport.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The 1935 Davson-Danielli model proposed protein-lipid-lipid-protein 'sandwich'.

By the 1970s evidence broke it: freeze-fracture EM showed proteins inside the bilayer, and fluorescent antibody labelling (Frye-Edidin, 1970) proved membranes are fluid.

Singer-Nicolson (1972) proposed the fluid mosaic — proteins floating in a 2D lipid sea.

Four key mechanisms:

- Simple diffusion — small non-polar (O₂, CO₂) cross freely.
- Osmosis — water through aquaporins, down water potential.
- Facilitated diffusion — ions/glucose via channels/carriers, passive.
- Active transport — Na⁺/K⁺ pump uses ATP, 3 Na⁺ out per 2 K⁺ in.

Large molecules cross by endocytosis (phagocytosis, pinocytosis) or exocytosis.

Membrane vesicles fuse with the plasma membrane, releasing contents — the basis of neurotransmitter release and hormone secretion.
